Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant life change you've recently experienced, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a screening tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and coping during this postpartum period. The purpose of this assessment is to get a better sense of your emotional well-being and identify any potential areas where we can offer additional support.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. The EPDS consists of 10 questions, and I'll ask them in a way that feels conversational and comfortable for you. Your responses will help me understand your experiences over the past week, and we'll use this information to identify any areas where you might need some extra support.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that this assessment is not a test, and there are no right or wrong answers. I'm here to listen and support you, and I want to encourage you to be as open and honest as you feel comfortable being. Are you ready to get started? Let's begin with the first question: Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself, and have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like to do?

.. I don't know, it's just been really tough lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'm tired all the time, and it's hard to find the energy to do anything. Even things that I used to love, like taking a walk or reading a book, just don't seem as enjoyable anymore. I mean, I'll try to do them, but it's just not the same. And with the baby, I feel like I'm just trying to keep up, you know? Make sure she's fed and bathed and all that. But as for me, I just feel... empty, I guess. And guilty, too. Like, I should be enjoying this time with my baby, but really, I'm just feeling really overwhelmed and anxious. Like, what if I'm not doing enough for her? What if I'm messing everything up? It's hard to explain. It's just been really hard to find any joy in things lately. (pausing, getting a bit choked up) Sorry... it's just been really tough.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I'll catch myself smiling or laughing at something the baby does, but it's not the same as it was before. It feels like it's just a surface-level happiness, you know? Like, I'm happy for a second, but then I'm right back to feeling anxious or overwhelmed. And it's hard to find the funny side of things when I'm so worried all the time. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and my mind will just start racing with all these worst-case scenarios... like, what if she chokes, or what if I'm not producing enough milk? It's hard to laugh when you're feeling like that. Sometimes, my husband will try to make me laugh, and I'll smile, but it's just not the same. I feel like I've lost my sense of humor, and it's really sad for me. (looking down, frowning) I just wish I could be myself again, you know?
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking my head) Not really. I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like another thing to worry about. Like, we'll plan a trip to the park, and I'll start thinking about all the things that could go wrong... what if the baby gets too hot, or what if I forget the diapers? It's hard to enjoy thinking about the future when I'm so caught up in worrying about the present. And even when I do try to look forward to something, it's just not the same. I'll think, "Oh, we're going to have a nice dinner tonight," and then I'll start worrying about how I'm going to get the baby to sleep, or whether I'll have enough energy to cook. It's like, I'm just going through the motions, but I'm not really enjoying anything. (sighing) Even things that I used to love, like spending time with my friends, just feel like a chore now. I'll think, "Oh, I should call Sarah," but then I'll worry about how I'll manage the baby while we're on the phone, or whether I'll be able to have a conversation without getting interrupted. It's just... everything feels so overwhelming. (looking down, feeling a bit tearful)
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, feeling a lump in my throat) Oh, yeah... that's definitely been me lately. I mean, if the baby cries, I'm like, "What did I do wrong? Is she hungry? Is she tired? Is it because I didn't burp her right?" And even if it's not my fault, I'll still find a way to blame myself. Like, the other day, the baby spit up all over her clothes, and I was like, "I should have been more careful with her feeding position." Or, if she's fussy, I'll think, "I must be doing something wrong, I'm not a good mother." It's like, I'm always questioning myself and my abilities as a mother. And it's not just with the baby, either. If I have a bad day, or if I don't get everything done that I wanted to, I'll beat myself up over it. I'll think, "I'm such a failure, I'm not doing enough, I'm not good enough." It's like, I'm my own worst critic, and it's really hard to shake that feeling. (looking down, feeling a bit ashamed) I just wish I could be kinder to myself, you know? But it's hard when you're already feeling so overwhelmed and anxious. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard to talk about this stuff.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, that's me all the time. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll start worrying about something ridiculous, like what if the house catches on fire, or what if someone breaks in. Or, I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll start thinking about all the things that could go wrong with the baby's health, like what if she has a rare disease, or what if she gets hurt. It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I have no control over it. And the thing is, I know it's irrational, I know it's not based in reality, but I just can't seem to shake it off. (rubbing my temples) It's like, my brain is just constantly on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's exhausting, because I'm always on edge, always waiting for the other shoe to drop. (sighing) Even when everything is fine, and the baby is happy and healthy, I still can't seem to relax. I'm just always waiting for something to go wrong. (looking up, feeling a bit tearful) It's like, I'm trapped in this constant state of anxiety, and I don't know how to escape it.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(taking a deep breath, nodding) Yes... that's happened to me too. I'll be doing something completely normal, like changing the baby's diaper or making lunch, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's like, my body is reacting like there's some kind of emergency, but there's no reason for it. (shaking my head) It's really scary, because I don't know what's happening or how to make it stop. And it's not just when I'm alone, either. Sometimes it happens when I'm with my husband or family members, and they'll be like, "What's wrong?" And I'm like, "I don't know, I just feel really scared all of a sudden." (looking down, feeling a bit embarrassed) It's hard to explain, because it doesn't make any sense. But it's like, my body is just on high alert all the time, waiting for something to go wrong. (pausing, taking a deep breath) And sometimes, it's not just a feeling of panic, it's also a feeling of... hopelessness, I guess. Like, I'll be thinking, "What's the point of any of this?" or "I'm never going to be able to do this." (looking up, feeling a bit tearful) It's a really dark and scary place to be, and I don't know how to get out of it.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, feeling overwhelmed) Yes, that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner and friend... it all just feels so overwhelming. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to make breakfast, and the baby will start crying, and I'll spill the coffee, and it's just... (throwing up my hands) it's too much. I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and if one more thing goes wrong, I'll just lose it. (sighing) And it's not just the practical things, it's the emotional stuff too. I feel like I'm supposed to be this perfect, happy mom, but really I'm just struggling to keep my head above water. I feel guilty for feeling overwhelmed, like I'm not doing enough or being enough. (looking down, feeling a bit ashamed) It's like, I'm just trying to survive, but I'm not really living. And that's a hard thing to admit, because I feel like I'm supposed to be grateful for this new baby and this new life, but really I'm just feeling... (pausing, searching for the right words) lost, I guess. Like, I don't know who I am anymore or how to do this.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a sense of relief that someone is acknowledging my struggles) Yes, that's been me lately. I'll lie in bed at night, and my mind will just start racing with all these thoughts and worries. I'll think about the baby, and whether I'm doing everything right, and whether I'm a good mom. And then I'll start thinking about all the things I need to do the next day, and how I'm going to get everything done. (sighing) It's like, my brain just won't shut off. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll be wide awake, thinking about all the same things. It's like, I'm trapped in this cycle of anxiety and worry, and I don't know how to escape it. (rubbing my eyes, feeling tired) I've been getting maybe 4 or 5 hours of sleep a night, and it's just not enough. I feel like I'm running on empty, and I don't know how to refill my tank. (looking up, feeling a bit desperate) I just want to be able to sleep again, to be able to rest and feel refreshed. But it's hard when your mind is racing all the time. (pausing, taking a deep breath) And it's not just the lack of sleep, it's the quality of sleep too. I'll have these vivid dreams, or nightmares, and I'll wake up feeling anxious and on edge. It's like, my body is just constantly stressed, even when I'm trying to rest. (shaking my head) It's exhausting, both physically and emotionally.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, feeling a lump in my throat) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness, and I don't know why. It's like, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying. Or, I'll be doing something completely normal, like laundry or dishes, and I'll just feel this wave of misery wash over me. (sighing) It's hard to explain, because it's not like anything specific is wrong. The baby is healthy, my husband is supportive, we have a roof over our heads... it's just... (shrugging) I don't know, it's like I'm just feeling really down, all the time. (looking down, feeling a bit ashamed) And it's hard, because I feel like I should be happy. I mean, I just had a baby, and that's supposed to be this joyful time, right? But really, I'm just feeling... (pausing, searching for the right words) empty, I guess. Like, I'm just going through the motions, but I'm not really feeling anything. (looking up, feeling a bit tearful) And it's scary, because I don't know how to make it stop. I don't know how to make myself feel better. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes, I'll have these thoughts, like... (pausing again, hesitating) like, what's the point of all this? Or, like, I'm just not cut out to be a mom. (looking down, feeling a bit ashamed) And that's a really hard thing to admit, because it feels like I'm failing, somehow. But it's just... (sighing) it's how I'm feeling, I guess.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, feeling a lump in my throat) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of emotion, and I'll just start crying. Sometimes it's because I'm feeling overwhelmed, and sometimes it's just because I'm feeling really sad. (wiping away a tear) It's hard, because I feel like I'm losing control, you know? I'll be in the middle of doing something, and I'll just start crying, and I won't be able to stop. (sighing) It's embarrassing, too, because sometimes my husband will be like, "What's wrong?" And I'll be like, "I don't know, I just am." (laughing slightly) It's like, I'm just a big ball of emotions, all the time. (looking down, feeling a bit ashamed) And it's not just the crying, it's the feeling of being out of control, too. Like, I'll be thinking, "Okay, I've got this, I can handle this," and then suddenly I'll just be overcome with emotion, and I'll be like, "No, I don't have this at all." (shaking my head) It's really hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be strong, and I'm supposed to be able to handle all of this. But really, I'm just struggling, a lot. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I think it's happened maybe once or twice a week, where I'll just have a big cry, and I won't be able to stop. And it's not just when I'm alone, either. Sometimes I'll be with my husband, or with friends, and I'll just start crying, and I'll be like, "I'm sorry, I don't know what's wrong with me." (looking up, feeling a bit tearful) It's just really hard, you know?
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pause, taking a deep breath, looking down) Yes... I have had those thoughts. (pausing again, struggling to find the right words) It's like, sometimes I'll be feeling really overwhelmed, and I'll just think, "What's the point of all this?" or "I don't know how to do this anymore." And then, sometimes, I'll have these thoughts, like... (pausing again, hesitating) like, what if I just didn't exist anymore? Or, what if I just wasn't here to deal with all of this? (looking up, feeling a bit ashamed) It's like, I know it's not a healthy thought, and I know it's not something I would ever act on, but it's just... (sighing) it's like, my mind is just so tired, and it's looking for a way out, I guess. (looking down, feeling a bit tearful) It's scary, because I don't want to feel that way. I want to be happy, and I want to be able to enjoy my life, and my baby. But sometimes, it just feels like too much. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I think it's happened maybe once or twice in the past week, where I've had those thoughts. And it's not like I'm planning anything, or that I would ever act on it. It's just... (shrugging) it's like, my mind is just in a really dark place, sometimes. (looking up, feeling a bit desperate) I just wish I could make it stop. I wish I could just feel happy, and fulfilled, and like I'm doing okay. But right now, I just feel... (pausing, searching for the right words) lost, I guess. Like, I don't know how to get out of this place, or how to make myself feel better.

* Loss of enjoyment in previously pleasurable activities
